Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today met Governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation, Kazuhiko Amakawa, on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok. The two sides discussed expanding cooperation in clean energy, semiconductors and critical minerals. In a social media post, Finance Ministry said, the discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in energy transition, advanced manufacturing, electric mobility and resilient supply chains. They also explored cooperation through the 600-million-dollar India-Japan Fund and Japanese participation in the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund.During the meeting, Ms Sitharaman encouraged Japanese investors to explore opportunities in data centres in Tier Two and Tier Three cities, including Visakhapatnam. She said such investments could help promote more balanced urban development.Mr Amakawa highlighted the success of the India-Japan Fund in electric mobility and bioethanol. He also expressed hope for a follow-on fund and noted growing Japanese interest in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and data centres.The Finance Minister is on a five-day official visit to Bangkok in Thailand, till 18th of this month to attend the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings.

. Former Indian spinner Ramesh Powar has been appointed as a member of the senior selection committee of the Indian men’s cricket team. According to an official statement, Pragyan Ojha will head the committee based on his seniority among the committee members. Accordingly, the senior Men’s Selection Committee now comprises Pragyan Ojha, Shiv Sundar Das, RP Singh, Ajay Ratra and Ramesh Powar.The BCCI said the decision to appoint Ramesh Powar was taken at a meeting of the Cricket Advisory Committee held earlier today. Mr. Powar has represented India in two Tests and 31 ODIs during his playing career. He has also held a coaching role for Indian women’s team besides being a bowling coach at the BCCI Centre of Excellence.The BCCI also showed appreciation for Mr. Ajit Agarkar for his commitment, conviction and contribution during his tenure as Chairman of the Men’s Selection Committee. Since his appointment in July 2023, Agarkar led the committee through a significant period for Indian cricket, with India winning three ICC trophies, two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games gold medals. He retired earlier this month.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the PM Jan Dhan Yojana.Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s financial inclusion journey since its launch in 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. With over 59 crore Jan Dhan accounts, the scheme has grown into the largest financial inclusion initiative in the world. The scheme has provided universal banking access for every household and has become the foundation for direct benefit transfers. It has helped save almost 3.5 lakh crore rupees by plugging leakages in welfare delivery.Addressing the centenary celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce in New Delhi last month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had said that Jan Dhan Yojana has transformed India’s banking landscape and today almost every family in the country is connected to the banking system.As the world’s largest financial inclusion initiative, the scheme is redefining access to banking for millions of underprivileged citizens. The Jan Dhan account holder can avail overdraft facility of up to ten thousand rupees per household.

. Global crude oil prices rose today. Brent crude was trading half a per cent up at 106 US dollars and 46 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.2 per cent up at 98 US dollars and 18 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Give It Up Campaign.The Give It Up campaign, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2015, has encouraged consumers to voluntarily give up their LPG subsidies. Under the campaign, more than one crore 13 lakh LPG consumers have voluntarily surrendered their LPG subsidy. The savings helped provide LPG connections to poor households under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, particularly benefiting rural women who relied on firewood and cow dung for cooking. The government has provided over ten crore 56 lakh free LPG connections under the scheme to adult women from poor households across the country. Addressing the Delhi Economics Conclave in 2015, Prime Minister Modi highlighted that the Give It Up movement inspired the citizens to come together to help underprivileged families acquire clean fuel.A resident of Uttar Pradesh, Sanju Devi said that the gas stove has made cooking much more convenient and freed her from exposure to smoke.The Give It Up campaign has promoted a sense of social responsibility among citizens and has supported the government’s efforts to ensure clean cooking fuel access for all.

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh’s  RSS Chief Dr. Mohan Bhagwat today said that a wave originating in the West is seeking to destroy values of decency, auspiciousness, culture and humanity across the world, including India. He said that even the so-called developed countries are facing the impact of this wave and feel helpless.Addressing the annual Vijayadashami Utsav celebrations of the RSS  at Reshimbagh ground in Nagpur this morning, Dr. Bhagwat said that forces seeking to dismantle the country are working with planned strategies. He cautioned that regime-change agitations do not resolve fundamental problems, warning that protests could become instruments of political interests and fuel divisions in society rather than delivering solutions.Referring to recent public agitation across the world and India, Dr. Bhagwat saidthat, peoplealso have a responsibility to contribute to the functioning of society and the country, driven by a sense of belonging and the conviction that the nation and society are their own. He said that this spirit should also guide public movements. However, when movements become instruments of political gain and are driven by hostility towards individuals, groups or ideologies, forces seeking to weaken India take advantage of this situation.Earlier today, Mr Bhagwat performedShastrapujanto mark theVijaydashmiUtsav.

. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will arrive in Mumbai today for an official visit to India. Shortly after his arrival, Secretary Rubio will pay tribute to victims of terror during a solemn wreath-laying ceremony at the Taj Memorial inside the historic Hotel Taj Mahal Palace. Mr Rubio willhold bilateralmeeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai this afternoon. The dialogue is expected to cover key aspects of the India-US strategic partnership, economic cooperation, regional stability and energy security. Later in the evening, Secretary Rubio is scheduled to attend the “Freedom 250 Reception” at the Jio World Convention Centre, celebrating key milestones in US history and bilateral diplomatic ties.Tomorrow, Secretary Rubio will complete the Mumbai leg of his visit andemplanefor Jamnagar in Gujarat.Earlier yesterday, Mr Rubio indicated that the US-India trade deal is close to finalisation. Speaking to reporters in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, he also defended Washington’s decision to temporarily waive sanctions for countries importing Russian oil and gas, saying the move is aimed at easing pressure on global energy supplies and prices. He said every country has to consider its own circumstances, including geography and the difficulty of sourcing energy from alternative suppliers. Rubio added that these factors must be weighed when making foreign policy decisions.This will be Mr Rubio’s second visit to India since May, when he attended the Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting hosted by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi.

. The French Open Super 750 badminton tournament will begin today in Paris. Indian shuttlers, led by two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu, will be eager to overcome their recent struggles and make a mark at the tournament. Sindhu will face South Korea’s top seed, An Se Young, in the women’s singles first round, while sixth seed Lakshya Sen will take on Japan’s Kodai Naraoka in his men’s singles opener. Former world No. 1 Kidambi Srikanth will look to build on his momentum as he faces compatriot Ayush Shetty in a clash between two generations. In men’s doubles, the Indian pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will face French brothers Christo Popov and Toma Junior Popov. The women’s doubles duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will take on Taiwan’s Lin Chih-Chun and Yang Chu Yun. In women’s singles, Tanvi Sharma and Isharani Baruah will face each other in an all-Indian first-round clash. Ashmita Chaliha will begin her campaign against China’s Han Qian Xi, while Unnati Hooda will take on Japan’s Riko Gunji.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues.Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through the FDI Policy.India’s foreign direct investment policy has undergone major reforms over the past decade, with the government liberalising sectoral rules to attract greater foreign investment into the country. The government has progressively liberalised FDI norms in key sectors, including defence, telecommunications, insurance and space. Foreign investment of up to 74 per cent is permitted in defence, 100 per cent in telecom, insurance and Space sector. The country has received a record over 748 billion US dollars in FDI between 2014 and 2025. The number of source countries investing in India also rose from 89 to 112. Addressing the Rozgar Mela in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted that today more than one hundred countries are investing in India through FDI.Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran said that India has opened up several sectors, including space, drones, defence and insurance, to foreign investment.The FDI policy reforms reflect India’s efforts to create a more investor-friendly environment, simplified investment procedures and to strengthen its position as a preferred global investment destination.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next three days. According to IMD, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience heavy rainfall today.MetDepartment has also predicted thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over East Rajasthan, Konkan, Goa, Lakshadweep, Madhya Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh today. Similar weather conditions are likely to prevail over Odisha, Rayalaseema, Telangana, Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka for the day.For Delhi, the Weather Agency has forecast a clear sky today.

Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.In 2023, Parliament passed the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act – Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, marking a historic milestone in its national journey to foster equitable representation of women in public life at all levels of the federal structure. This landmark legislation reserves one-third of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. In his Independence Day address this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to all political parties to end decades of delay and swiftly implement the one-third legislative reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies.Talking to Akashvani News, Rajya Sabha MP from Bihar Dharamshila Gupta said that through this act, the Modi government has paved the way for half of the country’s population to play a decisive role in political and policy-making processes.The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, once implemented, women’s representation will rise substantially in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies. It is a decisive step towards empowering India’s Nari Shakti with a stronger voice in decision-making and a greater role in shaping the nation’s future.

Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the semiconductor mission.Semiconductors are the building blocks of modern technology and a foundation of economic power. They power Artificial Intelligence (AI), telecommunications, electric mobility, defence and advanced manufacturing.  In the past two years, the global semiconductor market has grown by more than 20 per cent. 12 semiconductor projects have been approved across six states in the country, with investments commitments of more than one lakh 64 thousand crore rupees. Addressing SEMICON India 2026 in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India is taking every step needed to become a preferred destination for the semiconductor industry.Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, IT Expert Prasoon Sharma said India’s semiconductor journey is no longer a story of aspiration but is becoming a story of execution.India’s semiconductor journey has evolved from building strategic capabilities to creating a broader domestic ecosystem. These efforts are positioning India to participate across the semiconductor value chain.

The World Bank Group has launched its first comprehensive digital strategy, placing artificial intelligence, affordable internet access and job creation at the centre of its development agenda as 1.2 billion young people prepare to enter the workforce in developing countries over the next 10 to 15 years. Announced in Seoul today, the strategy brings together the institution’s public and private sector capabilities to help developing economies expand digital connectivity, improve access to technology and create employment opportunities. World Bank Group President Ajay Banga said the initiative would focus on practical applications of technology, particularly affordable artificial intelligence tools that can improve productivity and public services. The strategy identifies digital technology as a means of improving productivity and expanding employment in infrastructure, energy, agriculture, healthcare, tourism and manufacturing. The World Bank said more than two billion people remained offline globally in 2025.

In Asian Para Games, India has bagged 11 medals, including four gold, five silver and two bronze on day one of the tournament in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.Nishad Kumar clinched the India’s first para-athletics gold, winning the men’s long jump T47 event with a best effort of 7.11 meter.Soumya won gold in the women’s 1500m T12/T13 event, while Radha Venkatesh secured silver. While Ravanni Valasanaini won bronze in Women’s 1500m T11 event.In the men’s javelin F46 event, Rinku clinched gold and Ajeet Singh won silver.Earlier in the day, shooter Mona Agarwal claimed the gold with a Games record, while Avani Lekhara took the silver in the women’s 10 metre air rifle SH1 event in Nagoya.In Judo, Visually impaired judoka Kokila won silver medal in women’s J2 – 52kg Category. While Kapil Parmar won bronze in men’s J1 – 70 kg category.In para Swimming, Ravi Karthik won silver medal in men’s 100 m Freestyle S13 event. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the player on winning the medals.

A Houthi missile attack on a Military training centre in Yemen’s Shabwa governorate has killed more than 53 recruits and injured over 200 others, according to preliminary figures released by the Shabwa Governorate Media Office. In a statement issued today, the local authority said the recruits were undergoing training and security qualification at the Martyr Ahmed Al-Sulaimani Training Centre when it came under bombardment by several ballistic missiles.The authority condemned the attack, holding the Houthi militias responsible. It and called on Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council, government and coalition supporting the internationally recognised government to provide air defence systems and strengthen the governorate’s security capabilities. It also said medical resources had been mobilised to treat the injured, with critical cases to be transferred to specialised centres if necessary.The spokesperson for the Yemeni government’s armed forces, Majed Al Nuzaili informed on X that the Houthis fired three ballistic missiles at the centre.The Houthis have recently targeted various sites in government-held areas of Yemen, including the airport and presidential palace in Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised Yemen government.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has said that cargo movement on inland waterways increased from 29 million metric tonnes in 2014-15 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, registering a compound annual growth rate of 20.13 per cent. The Ministry said the growth has already surpassed the target of 200 million metric tonnes set under Maritime India Vision 2030. India has 111 National Waterways, extending over 20,187 kilometres across 23 states and four Union Territories. The Ministry added that the country is strengthening its inland waterway network through hydrographic surveys, modern navigation infrastructure and digital information systems to support the growing movement of cargo on rivers..

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives aimed at removing the colonial mindset.The history of modern India is deeply entangled with two centuries of British colonialism, and decades after Independence. Over the past few years, the Government has slowly been steering India, away from these vestiges of British rule. Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 76th Independence Day in 2022, the Prime Minister outlined five resolutions, or Panch Pran for the next 25 years. Elaborating on the second Praan, he said, in no part of citizens’ existence, not even in the deepest corners of mind or habits should there be any ounce of slavery.In a concerted effort to free the country from its colonial legacy and promote a distinct Indian identity, the Government has undertaken a series of initiatives across various sectors. the historic Rajpath in New Delhi was renamed Kartavya Path and inaugurated by the Prime Minister in 2022.  Similarly, a grand statue of freedom fighter Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was installed near India Gate, which has replaced the statue of King George the Fifth. The Indian Navy also adopted a new ensign in 2022, replacing the earlier design that featured the Saint George’s Cross. The Government has merged the Rail Budget with the Union Budget from budget year 2017-18, ending a practice dating back to 1924. BJP leader Ram Madhav has said that restoring India’s cultural and civilizational identity is a symbol of self-respect. He added that decolonisation is the real patriotism that is happening today.The Government has further sought to revive literature banned during British rule, with the National Archives of India compiling a catalogue of banned poems, writings and publications from the freedom struggle. In addition, more than 1,500 obsolete laws have been repealed in recent years as part of efforts to simplify governance and remove outdated legal provisions.These initiatives reflect the Government’s stated commitment to building a confident, self-reliant India rooted in its cultural heritage and national values.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated para athlete Rinku on winning the Gold Medal and Ajeet Singh on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s Javelin F46 event at the Asian Para Games 2026. The President said that Rinku’s throw has carried the Indian Tricolour to the top of the podium and brought immense pride to the nation. She said that this achievement will inspire aspiring javelin throwers to aim farther.The President also congratulated Soumya on winning the Gold Medal and Radha Venkatesh on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s 1500m T12/13 event. She expressed hope that they will continue to pursue their sporting goals with full confidence, and will get many more opportunities in the future to showcase their talent on the track.President Murmu has also extended her wishes to Nishad Kumar on winning the Gold Medal in the Men’s Long Jump T47 event. She said that this remarkable success highlights his versatility and willingness to take on new challenges.The President also congratulated Ravi K. Budigina on securing the Silver Medal in the Men’s 100m Freestyle S13 at the Games. She wished that this achievement will inspire aspiring swimmers to take the plunge and pursue their ambitions with conviction.She also congratulated Kokila on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s Judo J2 -52kg category and Kapil Parmar on winning the Bronze Medal in Para Judo at the Games. She said that this success will inspire them to continue striving for excellence and reach even greater heights in their sporting journey.President Droupadi Murmu also congratulated Mona Agarwal on winning the Gold Medal in the Women’s 10 meter Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the Asian Para Games 2026. In a social media post, the President appreciated the efforts of the athlete for setting a new Asian Para Games record. She also expressed confidence that her achievement will inspire many to dream big. President Murmu also emphasised that even the most ambitious dreams can be realised with determination and hard work.She also congratulated Avani Lekhara on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the Games. President Murmu wished her best for the future and expressed hope that her sporting journey will continue to provide her with new opportunities to excel and fulfill her aspirations.

. Domestic investors are set to navigate a week packed with key market drivers, including macroeconomic data, corporate earnings results, and geopolitical developments. Market sentiment will also be driven by foreign institutional investor (FII) flows, commodity prices, bond yield movements, and currency fluctuations during the holiday-shortened week ahead.Indian equity markets will remain closed on Tuesday on account of Dussehra. Market participants will closely track the country’s core industries growth figures and forex reserves data. On the primary market front, two mainboard IPOs are set to open for subscription, including one of the biggest IPOs in India so far.Globally, investors will closely monitor developments surrounding the West Asia conflict. Bank of South Korea is scheduled to declare its monetary policy decision. In Japan, inflation data will be on focus along with an eye on China’s third quarter GDP estimates and industrial production data.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.3 per cent up at 1,46,426 rupees per 10 grams. Silver surged over 1.2 per cent to 2,10,918 rupees per kilogram.

. The Election Commission has shared FAQs on electoral process saying that Special Intensive Revision (SIR) seeks to ensure that no eligible Indian citizen is excluded from the electoral roll. It added that the aim of the exercise is to identify and remove any invalid entries like those relating to deceased persons, duplicate registrations, permanently shifted electors, foreigners and persons otherwise ineligible for electoral registration, in accordance with the prescribed legal procedure.The Commission added that the last major intensive revisions were undertaken during 2002-2004 and after more than two decades, comprehensive verification is necessary to maintain the accuracy, integrity and credibility of electoral rolls. On eligiblity, the Commission said that under Article 326 of the Constitution, only Indian citizens are eligible to be registered as voters. The SIR  process begins with house-to-house verification, followed by the publication of draft rolls and then claims and objections are invited and before the publication of Final Electoral Roll, a notice and hearing phase is carried out.The Poll Body further stated that Special Summary Revision (SSR)  has been rolled out in 17 States and UTs, all of which have already completed SIR. It added that the SSR instructions issued on 15th of this month is different from ongoing SIR as both are different exercises aiming at ensuring a pure and updated electoral roll.On Electronic Voting Machines- EVMs, the Commission clarified that EVMs can not  be hacked or remotely manipulated through the internet,Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or mobile phones. It said, the Commission’s  EVMs are standalone devices without internet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or mobile-network connectivity and remote manipulation through those channels is not supported by their design.

. At the Asian Para Games, India won two silver medals in Aichi, Nagoya, Japan, today.In the men’s65kgpowerlifting event, India’s Ashok won the silver medal with a best lift of 192kg. China’s reigning Paralympic champion Zou Yi claimed gold with 216kg, while Indonesia’s Margono secured bronze with 177kg.In the men’s 10m air pistol SH1 event, Indian para shooter Manish Narwal won silver, scoring 233.7 points in the final. South Korea’s Jo Jeongdu won gold while China’s Yang Chao took bronze with 213.6 points.Earlier, Indian para-athlete Deepthi Jeevanji clinched gold in the women’s 400m T20 event, setting a new Games record with a time of 56.36 seconds. Jeevanji’s medal marked India’s fifth gold medal.Indian para-table tennis players Baby Sahana Ravi and Prachi Pandey won bronze medals in the women’s singles Class 9 and Class 6 events. With Baby Sahana Ravi and Prachi Pandey winning bronze medals, India secured four medals in para table tennis on the same day.Bhavina Patel secured a bronze medal after facing a 3-0 defeat to China’s Zhang Bian in the Women’s Singles Class 4-5 semi-finals. Sonalben Patel also secured a bronze in the women’s singles Class 3 event after losing her semi-final against South Korea’s Yoon Jiyu in straight games, 7-11, 5-11, 6-11.

. In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by nine paise to close at 94.96 rupees against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.66 in intra-day trade.

. The festival of Vijaya Dashmi and Dussehra, which marks the triumph of good over evil, is being celebrated across the nation today. This joyous day marks the culmination of the nine-day Navratri festival and the grand Durga Puja celebrations. The ceremonial Ravana Dahan, or burning of effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna, and Meghanada, also takes place today. Durga Puja festivities conclude on Vijaya Dashami with Durga Visarjan, the ceremonial immersion of the goddess’s idols into rivers, lakes, or artificial water bodies. In the National Capital Delhi, effigies of Ravana, Kumbhkarna and Meghnad will be burnt at different places.People also perform Ayudha Puja to bless their tools of trade and books, treating it as an incredibly auspicious time to start new businesses, education, or creative ventures.

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined over 8.5 billion US dollars (USD) to 726 billion US dollars during the week ended 9th of October. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 7.1 billion dollars to 597.6 billion dollars during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 1.3 billion dollars to 105 billion dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 109 million dollars to 18.5 billion dollars. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped 10 million dollars to 4.78 billion dollars.

. India’s youngest National Karting Champion Arshi Gupta has become world’s youngest driver to win the Rotax MAX Challenge (RMC) Mini title. She won the Mini Max category of The Federation of Motor Sports Clubs of India- FMSCI RMC India National Karting Championship 2026 held in Bengaluru yesterday.The title follows Arshi’s 2025 triumph in the Micro Max category, making her one of the rare drivers to win two successive Rotax MAX Challenge categories in consecutive years. Speaking at a press conference in New Delhi today, 10 year old Arshi who is from Faridabad shared her journey, achievements and ambitions in motorsports. She expressed her happiness at winning the Indian National Karting Championship 2025 and 2026.Arshi is the youngest driver globally to be selected for the F1 Academy Discover Your Drive programme, a recipient of the FIA President’s Medal, and a podium finisher in the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom.

US President Donald Trump has signalled his willingness to hold a high-stakes trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine and pursuing global denuclearisation, even if Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is excluded from the negotiations. Speaking to reporters at the White House before departing for Kansas, Trump said he would be willing to meet with the Russian and Chinese leaders to help broker peace and curb nuclear proliferation. Earlier on Sunday, an American newspaper reported that Putin had proposed holding a trilateral summit with Trump and Xi next month to discuss the Ukraine conflict, with the aim of negotiating a peace deal favourable to Moscow.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like Jan Bhagidari.Jan Bhagidari, which means public participation, is a core governance model under Narendra Modi government. Schemes that utilize the Jan Bhagidari model include Swachh Bharat  Mission, Catch the Rain, Vocal for Local, and Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. Citizens in India had traditionally been treated as passive beneficiaries of government schemes. Jan Bhagidari has brought a change to this and fostered local ownership and behavioural change in people. Prime Minister Narendra Modi regularly highlights Jan Bhagidari as a core pillar of nation-building through his monthly radio program, Mann Ki Baat. In Mann Ki Baat  last month, Prime Minister Modi again highlighted Jan Bhagidari as a driving force for social change, urging citizens to join collective movements like the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan.Talking to Akashvani News, Shivendra Singh, a resident of Prayagraj, spoke about how he and his family and friends believe in Jan Bhagidari and go Vocal For Local during festive seasons.Participation has now become ownership of transformation happening around the country, with the people becoming stakeholders in national development.

Vice Chief of the Naval Staff Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar today highlighted the importance of durable indigenous technologies for combat readiness, operational flexibility and sustained capability enhancement.Vice Admiral Kochhar was addressing the Curtain Raiser Press Conference for the fifth edition of the Indian Navy’s flagship Naval Innovation and Indigenisation Seminar, Swavlamban 2026 in New Delhi. He remarked that the evolution of Swavlamban since 2022 has connected the Indian Navy’s operational requirements with the technological capabilities of Indian industry and academia. Emphasising the changing character of modern warfare, he underscored the importance of developing niche technologies into deployable systems at sea.The two day annual NIIO Seminar Swavlamban wiil begin on monday in New Delhi. Swavlamban 2026 will build upon the Indian Navy’s continuing efforts to translate indigenous technological innovation into operational capabilities and strengthen the foundations of Aatmanirbharta. The seminar will bring together innovators, industry partners, Start-ups, MSMEs, academia, investors and the Defence Forces to explore collaborative solutions for emerging maritime security challenges.The exhibition at Swavlamban 2026 will include thematic areas, showcasing indigenous innovations that have emerged as success stories, covering niche technologies in Maritime Surveillance, Counter-UAS, Artificial Intelligence and Quantum, Safety and Efficiency Enhancers. Engagements with venture capitalists and investors will form a key component of the seminar, facilitating discussions on funding opportunities, scaling of promising enterprises and commercialisation of indigenous technologies. This year’s seminar will provide a dynamic platform for deliberations on future and emerging technologies with transformative potential to enhance naval operations and strengthen India’s maritime capabilities.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like GST Council.Introduced on 1STJuly, 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) marked a significant milestone in India’s tax reform journey. By bringing multiple Central and State taxes under a unified framework, GST gave effect to the principle of One Nation, One Tax and paved the way for a more integrated and streamlined taxation system across the country. The proposals of the GST Council seek to create a more predictable and taxpayer-friendly GST registration framework. Under the next-generation GST reforms last year, the GST council had simplified the earlier four-tier structure of 5 per cent, 12 percent, 18 percent, 28 percent into a two tier structure of 5 percent and 18 percent. Addressing the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that through GST, the government has transformed a complex web of taxes into a national market.Addressing media after the 58thGST Council meeting in New Delhi, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the Council   recommended removing arrest powers under GST, raising the prosecution threshold from one crore to five crore rupees.Over the past nine years, standardised procedures and rationalised rates have supported greater transparency, accountability and economic growth and strengthened the vision of ‘Ek Bharat – Shreshtha Bharat’.

. India’s visually impaired judoka Kokila has assured herself of a medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya after defeating China’s Yi Liu 1-0 in the women’s J2 -52kg semifinal. She will face Kyrgyzstan’s Aibike Ulanbek Kyzy in the final later in the day, with gold at stake.Kokila, who won bronze in the -48kg category at the previous edition in Hangzhou, hails from Haryana’s Jind district and represented India at the Paris 2024 Paralympics.In the men’s J1 -70kg category, Kapil Parmar will compete for bronze after losing 0-1 to Indonesia’s Junaedi in the semifinal. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Indian shooter Mona Agarwal on winning Gold in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the Asian Para Games 2026.In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that her remarkable achievement has made India’s opening day even more special. Mr Modi said that her precision, determination and composure are truly commendable. He also lauded her outstanding score for setting a new Asian Para Games Record and wished her continued success in the competitions ahead.The Prime Minister also congratulated Avani Lekhara on winning Silver in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Standing SH1 event at the Asian Para Games 2026 with an impressive score. . India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) comes into force on the occasion of Vijay Dashami today. The agreement will provide duty-free access for 100 per cent of Indian exports to New Zealand. Addressing a ceremony on India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement in New Delhi, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that the agreement is aligned with the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for Viksit Bharat 2047. Hesaid, theagreement opens significant new opportunities for India’s exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers and pharma. The Minister highlighted that both the countries have agreed to work towards the goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services with New Zealand to approximately 35 thousand crore rupees by 2030.Mr Goyal said that India’s farmers will gain wider market access for fruits, vegetables, spices and other agricultural produce. Hesaid, theagreement will help improve productivity, support higher incomes and strengthen livelihoods. The Minister highlighted that sensitive sectors, including dairy, remain protected, keeping farmers’ welfare at the heart of the government’s approach.The Minister said that New Zealand’s commitment to facilitate 20 billion US dollars in investment into India holds immense potential to strengthen manufacturing, infrastructure, services and innovation. Mr Goyal said, this agreement will also create employment opportunities. He expressed confidence that this win-win partnership will achieve many more milestones, guided by the shared vision of growth and mutual prosperity between the two nations.The FTA between India and New Zealand was signed in April this year at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Agreement will create new opportunities in services, investment and professional, student and youth mobility, including enhanced pathways for Indian professionals and students. India and New Zealand share longstanding and close relations, anchored in strong people-to-people ties and expanding cooperation across trade and investment, agriculture, education, sports, technology and other areas. The Bilateral merchandise trade between India and New Zealand stood at around 1.1 billion US dollars in 2025-26. The FTA represents a significant step in further strengthening these ties and creating new opportunities for businesses and communities in both countries.On the occasion, the first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off by Mr Goyal. Flag-offs of a range of products across the agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather sectors are also planned for the day. These initiatives reflect the confidence of Indian manufacturers and the opportunities the Agreement opens up for exporters across the country.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the International Solar Alliance.India and France had jointly launched the International Solar Alliance in November 2015 during the COP21 climate conference. The global intergovernmental organisation is dedicated to accelerating the deployment of solar energy as a pathway to energy access, energy security, and sustainable development. ISA was created to mobilise collective action against climate change through the widespread adoption of solar energy solutions.  Today, ISA has evolved into a global platform for international cooperation on solar energy, with 129 countries currently registered as members. Co-chairing the launch of International Solar Alliance during COP21 in Paris, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the alliance focuses on making solar energy cheap, reliable, and widely accessible by driving research and development, streamlining regulations, building infrastructure, and unlocking new financing models to draw investment.Talking to Akashvani News, Director General of International Solar Alliance Ashish Khanna said that ISA signifies the strength of the vision of  Prime Minister Modi and showcases India’s ability to the global south, bringing together countries for cleaner energy, livelihood and energy security.The alliance represents a transformative movement towards a sustainable energy future. With India leading this initiative, ISA not only aims to enhance energy access and security but focuses to significantly reduce carbon emissions globally.

The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) will organise its annual Vijayadashami celebrations at Reshimbagh ground in Nagpur this morning as part of the concluding year of the organisation’s centenary celebrations.RSS Sarsanghchalak Dr. Mohan Bhagwat will deliver the keynote address.The programme will begin with a route march of Swayamsevaks and Shastra Pujan.One of the largest social organisations of the world, RSS was founded in Nagpur by its First Sarsanghchalak, Dr. Keshav Hedgewar, in 1925 on the occasion ofVijayadashmi.

. Ekta Vishnoi has won three gold medals at the World Masters Classic and Equipped Powerlifting Championships in Nevada, USA. She claimed the top honours in the 57kg category with a combined lift of 362.5kg. She lifted 130 kg in squat, 72.5 kg in bench press and 160 kg in deadlift, finishing ahead of competitors from Canada and Japan. Vishnoi won gold in the squat, deadlift and overall total categories. Ms. Vishnoi an Indian Revenue Service officer, has previously led the Fit India Mission and served as Deputy Director General of the Sports Authority of India.

. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar will also hold talks with UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Mumbai today. The two Foreign Ministers are also expected to deliberate on the overall situation in West Asia, including the recent attacks on Saudi Arabia. External Affairs Minister spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the meeting between the two leaders will be an opportunity to review all facets of bilateral cooperation and discuss the situation in West Asia, as well as global and multilateral issues. Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan arrived in Mumbai yesterday evening to further strengthen the bilateral partnership between the two nations. He was received and welcomed by Mangalprabhat Lodha, Maharashtra’s Minister for Skill Development.

. Paris policehasimposed an overnight curfew in two areas of the French capital following a weekend of severe rioting that targeted city halls, other public buildings and thousands of businesses across the country. The unrest was among France’s worst in years. The order, issued yesterday, aims to protect people and property from violence and looting. It prohibits people from entering or remaining in Place de la République, where rioting broke out on Saturday, and the shopping district of Les Halles, which was targeted by looters. The curfew will remain in effect from 11 pm yesterday until 6 am today. Paris police also announced a ban on gatherings and demonstrations from 8 pm.

. In Women’s Cricket, the third and final T20 International between India and Zimbabwe will be played at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Stadium in Raipur today. The match will begin at 7 PM IST, with the hosts looking to complete a clean sweep in their first-ever bilateral women’s T20I series against Zimbabwe. The series also marks a new chapter for India under full-time captain Smriti Mandhana, who will aim to build momentum ahead of the upcoming ODI series. India defeated Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the second T20 match on Sunday, taking an unassailable 2-NIL lead in the series. This is the first bilateral women’s Cricket series between India and Zimbabwe. The T20 series will be followed by a three-match One Day International series in Vadodara, with matches scheduled for the 23rd, 25th and 28th of this month.
